candidates.exact_span: permittee must collect an effluent composite sample volume during the period of discharge that is sufficient to complete the required toxicity tests with daily renewal of effluent, and must meet the holding time between collection and first use of the sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether toxicity monitoring was required during a given period depends on whether discharge occurred and whether sample volume and holding-time conditions were met; different readings of 'during the period of discharge' or sufficiency of the composite can change whether an obligation applied or whether absent/late results are treated as missing required evidence versus a documented no-discharge or non-applicable period.

candidates.exact_span: When possible, the effluent samples used for the toxicity tests shall be collected on separate days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'when possible' and whether separate-day collection was feasible affects whether the permittee had a monitoring-protocol obligation for a given test event and whether partial or single-day sampling satisfies the requirement.

candidates.exact_span: The effluent composite sample collection duration and the static renewal protocol associated with the abbreviated sample collection must be documented in the full report required in Item 3 of this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether documentation was a binding monitoring/reporting obligation for abbreviated collections affects Purpose B; for Purpose C, whether missing documentation establishes inadequate evidence, a documented protocol deviation, or an unresolved no-data state depends on how 'must be documented' and 'abbreviated sample collection' are interpreted against available reports.

candidates.exact_span: Test failure may not be construed or reported as invalid due to a coefficient of variation value of greater than 40%, or a PMSD value greater than the higher value on the range provided.
candidates.computation_change_reason: For Purpose A, treating a toxicity test as valid despite elevated CV or PMSD can change whether an enforceable limit comparison is performed and whether a reported failure counts as exceeding the limit; for Purpose C, the same rule distinguishes a usable numeric/compliance result from evidence that would otherwise be classified as invalid or missing.

candidates.exact_span: The statistical analyses used to determine if there is a significant difference between the control and the critical dilution shall be in accordance with the methods for determining the No Observed Effect Concentration (NOEC) as described in the appropriate method manual listed in Part II or the most recent update thereof.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which NOEC method manual and update apply, and how 'significant difference' is calculated, can change whether a toxicity measurement is deemed to pass or exceed the applicable enforceable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Dilution water used in the toxicity tests will be receiving water collected as close to the point of discharge as possible but unaffected by the discharge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether receiving water was collected sufficiently close and unaffected by the discharge affects test validity and thus Purpose A limit comparisons; it also bears on whether the permittee met required toxicity-test monitoring conditions under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span:
The permittee shall substitute synthetic dilution water of similar pH, hardness, and alkalinity to the closest downstream perennial water for;
               i. toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges to receiving water
                  classified as intermittent streams; and
              ii. toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is
                  available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of the receiving water as intermittent, and whether zero-flow conditions existed, gate both the monitoring protocol that was required and whether a period is documented as no-discharge/zero-flow (reducing or altering monitoring obligations) versus a case where standard receiving-water collection still applied.

candidates.exact_span:
If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests provided the unacceptable receiving water test met the following stipulations:
                i. a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance require-
                   ments was run concurrently with the receiving water control;
               ii. the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to
                   completion,
              iii. the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity
                   with the full report and information required; and
              iv. the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity
                   similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial
                   water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of
                   these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether substitution was permitted hinges on contested facts (instream toxicity, concurrent controls, test completion, reporting, and water-quality similarity); different interpretations change which toxicity results are admissible for limit comparison (A), whether alternate monitoring procedures were required or satisfied (B), and whether missing or substituted tests reflect documented conditional non-requirement, adequate evidence, or unresolved gaps (C).
